messages:
Maya R: Heads up — since the cu12 image rollout last night we started seeing a steady trickle of cold-start nodes failing to attach to NCCL rings during provisioning. Not huge volume yet but noisy.
Lin (infra): Seen it too. Symptoms: container starts, GPU visible in nvidia-smi, then nvml init logs a timeout and provider fails to register. Nodes go into provisioning retry loop.
Jordan: Is this the same as the modprobe timing/race we had before or something new? Any kernel oops?
Maya R: Not a kernel oops. Example from one host:
```
[init] loading nvidia: OK
[init] nvml_init() timeout after 10s
[provisioner] attach failed: nvml: NVML_ERROR_TIMEOUT
[provisioner] retrying (backoff)
```
Devon: We saw a cluster-wide ripple in eu-west-2 during the canary window — ~0.7% of spins hit it, but the provisioning backoff made capacity look lower than it was.
Sara: I have a 1-off that also included NCCL errors in logs after join timeout:
```
NCCL WARN Call to connect returned error 116 (Connection timed out)
NCCL INFO Ring id 3 failing, aborting
```
Lin (infra): Two hypotheses: 1) toolkit 12 changed driver probe/ordering causing NVML init to race against container network setup; 2) compiler runtime mismatch in the new images causing subtle ABI differences for nccl/libcuda calls.
Maya R: Agreed. Also noticed our container builder used host gcc-symlink during buildkit stage. Could be mixing libstdc++ from host into final image accidentally. That would manifest as weird runtime glue issues.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: canary rollout paused for cu12-image to eu-west-2 at 03:12 UTC (triggered by provisioner alerts).
Jordan: Immediate mitigations we can try:
- revert canary to cu11 for new spins
- increase provisioner parallelism so backoffs don't look like capacity loss
- add NVML init retry w/ longer timeout in the attach path
Which should be immediate?
Lin (infra): Reverting canary is lowest risk. We should also add a short-circuit in the scheduler to mark nodes 'warm' sooner so we don't route heavy joins immediately.
Devon: If we revert, we'll need to drain the bad images out of staging pools. That takes ~20–30m in ap-southeast and eu-west due to queued builds.
Sara: I ran a local repro with an instrumented shim: when network namespace bring-up is slow (dns/dhclient), NVML init hit the 10s timeout. Increasing to 30s made the repro go away. But that doesn't explain NCCL handshake timeouts — those point to ephemeral network packet loss during ring formation.
Maya R: Could be two separate but related problems: slower net bring-up causes NVML attach retries, and if some nodes fall behind, NCCL peer connect times out. Both amplify each other in provisioning bursts.
Jordan: Action items:
- revert canary to cu11 now (Lin)
- bump NVML attach timeout to 30s and land as feature flag (Maya)
- add short grace period before heavy NCCL joins for newly provisioned nodes (Devon)
- run a forced repro on a slow network bring-up testbed and capture packet traces (Sara)
Lin (infra): Revert started 03:22 UTC. OpsBot will announce when finished.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: cu12-canary revert to cu11 scheduled and started at 03:22 UTC. Estimated completion 03:45 UTC.
Maya R: I'll prepare a postmortem draft once we confirm repro and RCA. Early suspicion: toolkit packaging + build-time host toolchain leakage + provisioner timing assumptions. If true, we need stricter image hermeticity checks.
Devon: Also cost note — the backoff/retries increased startup token consumption for provisioner jobs by ~12% in eu-west-2 last night. If left unfixed, committed capacity penalties might spike on reserved pools.
Sara: Packet captures scheduled. I'll post logs in this thread when done.
Jordan: Thanks team — prioritize revert + telemetry for now. We'll sync in the 10:30 follow-up.
Maya R: 👍 will update here when we have traces or a confirmed RCA.
